markscheme.html:
C

The proper time interval between two events is, by definition, the time interval measured in a reference frame where the two events occur at the same spatial location. Due to time dilation, any observer moving relative to this frame will measure a longer time interval. Therefore, for observer X to measure the proper time, events P and Q must happen at the same point in space in X's frame.

question.html: An observer X measures the proper time interval between events P and Q. What must be true about this scenario?
